intent: Clarify the primitive ontology underlying RT orientation, admissibility, symmetry references, and observer-relative ordering without modifying RT_core.

summary.goal: Replace implicit motion-based intuition with an ordinal relational interpretation while preserving RT_core.

core_observations.title: Symmetry is Referential
core_observations.statement: Symmetry is not a force, attractor, optimizer, or cause. Symmetry is a reference condition against which relational organization is evaluated.

core_observations.title: Asymmetry is Relational
core_observations.statement: Asymmetry is not an independent primitive. It is the observable consequence of unequal exclusion relative to declared symmetry references.

core_observations.title: Primitive Distinction
core_observations.statement: The primitive distinction condition (*|*) permits distinction to exist but does not itself determine orientation.

core_observations.title: Affect|Effect
core_observations.statement: A|E is interpreted as the primitive relational condition undergoing evaluation relative to declared symmetry references.

symmetry_reference_model.meaning: A|E is evaluated relative to two declared symmetry references rather than attracted toward either.

orientation_model.primitive_claim: Orientation is determined by relational exclusion rather than attraction.
candidate_process: A|E evaluates relative to symmetry references.

exclusion_model.statement: Preference emerges because exclusion generally cannot remain perfectly balanced relative to both declared symmetry references simultaneously.

ordinal_update_model.motivation: Avoid treating motion and time as primitive.
ordinal_update_model.statement: Successive evaluations are interpreted as ordinal reorientations rather than spatial motion.
ordinal_update_model.interpretation: The ordering denotes relational precedence, not temporal progression.

observer_model.statement: Observation is a boundary interaction that reconstructs ordinal orientation changes.

jitter_interpretation.description: Candidate orientations continually fluctuate within the admissibility window.
jitter_interpretation.meaning: The continual relational re-evaluation of admissible orientations.
jitter_interpretation.explicit_note: The term 'superposition' is metaphorical only and does not invoke quantum state vectors.

rt_resolution_model.important_note: Undecided is not ignorance. It is a lawful evaluation state pending admissible orientation.

textbook_gap_analysis.identified_gap: Current textbook defines admissibility and arbitration but does not explicitly define the primitive relational condition producing orientation preference.
textbook_gap_analysis.candidate_resolution: Orientation preference arises through exclusion relative to declared symmetry references.

candidate_definitions.definition: Unequal exclusion relative to declared symmetry references.
Preferred relational organization produced by admissible exclusion.
Successive admissible orientation without requiring primitive time.

required_future_work: Determine whether distinction density mathematically governs exclusion.
Audit compatibility with all textbook chapters.
Determine whether arbitration becomes an operator acting upon exclusion rather than primitive selection.
governance_notes: Requires adversarial ontology audit before lexicon integration.
Should initially reside in Phase 0 ontology refinement.
